review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped it for @[simp] and for every use of the θ/ρ/Φ evaluation lemmas. The file has no simp attributes. The pressure points are the families of structural evaluation lemmas, which are only ever applied through hand-written `rw [...]` or `simp only [...]` chains. Mathlib's own AdjoinRoot.lift_of and lift_root are simp lemmas, which I did not look up in the Mathlib source, so that comparison is from memory. I found no rewrite loops or orientation problems. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that any suggested simp set would work or close the goals. One caveat is that the heavy explicit-argument signature of ρ and Φ should still allow unification, because every argument occurs in the lemma's left-hand side.

findings.excerpt: theorem Φ_root : Φ ϖ hϖm g h w hw hgm hhm e hgh (AdjoinRoot.root _) = gR g :=
findings.problem: These four lemmas are the canonical computation rules for the homomorphisms ρ and Φ on generators, namely `C a`, `X`, `AdjoinRoot.of F` and `AdjoinRoot.root`. None is a simp lemma. Every use re-spells the same rewrite chain by hand: `rw [map_add, map_mul, Φ_of, Φ_of, Φ_root]` appears at lines 772, 813 and 963, and `ρ_C, θW_ϖW` at lines 675, 811, 899, 906, 951 and 1032. The `simp only [... ρ_X, ρ_C, ...]` at line 620 has to list them explicitly. The duplicated `Φ_of, Φ_of` is brittle, since it depends on the number of occurrences.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `ρ_C`, `ρ_X`, `Φ_of` and `Φ_root` as `@[simp]`, as the corresponding AdjoinRoot.lift_of and lift_root lemmas are in Mathlib. Together with `map_add` and `map_mul`, the chains at lines 772, 813 and 963 can then become `simp only [map_add, map_mul, Φ_of, Φ_root]` or a plain `simp`. Each left-hand side is headed by the opaque definition ρ or Φ, so there is no loop or competing rule.
findings.benefit: Reduces the repeated, occurrence-count-sensitive `rw` chains. Anyone extending the argument gets the evaluation of ρ and Φ on generators automatically.

rw [map_add, map_mul, Φ_of, Φ_of, Φ_root, Algebra.smul_def, Algebra.smul_def, halg, mul_one]

findings.excerpt: PowerSeries.liftOfIsAdicComplete J θ x hx PowerSeries.X = x
findings.problem: The universal-property lemmas for the lift (`_coe`, `_C`, `_X`) are the intended simp interface for `liftOfIsAdicComplete`. The file is a generic API for a lift homomorphism, in the style of Mathlib's `lift` constructions. They are not simp lemmas, and every specialisation (`θ₀_C`, `θ₀_X`, `ρ_C`, `ρ_X`) is a hand-written forwarding lemma, `PowerSeries.liftOfIsAdicComplete_C _ _ _ _ a`. Consequently the simp set cannot compute `θ₀`, `ρ` and similar maps, and each specialisation has to be restated and then rewritten manually.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `liftOfIsAdicComplete_C` and `liftOfIsAdicComplete_X` with `@[simp]`. Tag `liftOfIsAdicComplete_coe` too if the polynomial coercion is wanted. Then, after unfolding the definitions, simp can compute `θ₀`, `ρ` and the other specialisations, and the forwarding lemmas can be marked `@[simp]` or replaced by `simp [θ₀]`.
findings.benefit: Provides one canonical normal form for evaluating the lift on constants and on X. Downstream specialisations no longer need hand-written copies.

findings.excerpt: theorem θW_ϖW : θW ϖ hϖm (ϖW ϖ) = ϖR (R := R) ϖ := by
findings.problem: `ϖW ϖ` and `ϖR` are reducible abbreviations, so `θW_ϖW` is the instance `a := ϖ` of `θW_const`. Both have the identical proof `rw [θW_mk, θ₀_C]`. Making any of these a simp lemma would put overlapping rules in the simp set: `θW_mk` (a general rule), `θW_const` (a more specific one) and `θW_ϖW` (the most specific). Callers currently choose between `θW_ϖW` (lines 584, 620, 675, 811, 899, 906, 1032) and `θW_const` (line 951) ad hoc for what is the same rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one canonical rule. The natural choice is `θW_const`, or just `θW_mk` plus `θ₀_C`. Drop `θW_ϖW`, or derive it as a one-line corollary of `θW_const`, and mark it simp only if the more specific lemma is deliberately kept. Use the same lemma at every call site.
findings.benefit: Avoids overlapping simp rules for the same expression, and gives the θW interface a single normal form for evaluation on constants.

findings.excerpt: abbrev IW : Ideal (PowerSeries O) := Ideal.span {(PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries O) - PowerSeries.C (ϖ ^ 1)}
findings.problem: The ideal `IW` is defined with the generator `X - C (ϖ ^ 1)`, which is not in simp normal form because `pow_one` rewrites `ϖ ^ 1` to `ϖ`. This leaks into the proofs. `mk_X_eq_ϖW` needs `simpa using ... (by rfl : ... C (ϖ ^ 1) ∈ _)` to rewrite on both sides, and the well-definedness proof of `θW` has to insert `pow_one` by hand (`rw [map_mul, map_sub, θ₀_X, pow_one, θ₀_C, ...]`). Any simp-based reasoning about membership of the generator would see a different expression from the one stored in `IW`.
findings.proposed_change: Define `IW` with the generator `X - C ϖ`. Do the conversion from the `^ 1` form once, in `W_facts`, for example by `simpa using PowerSeries.quotient_span_X_sub_C_pow_of_irreducible ϖ hϖ.out 1 le_rfl` or by a single `pow_one` rewrite. Then `mk_X_eq_ϖW` and `θW` no longer need `pow_one` or the `by rfl` ascription.
findings.benefit: The stored generator is already in canonical form, so simp and rw work on the real expression. This removes the scattered `pow_one` workarounds.
